item.text: {"question_id":"2B.1","answer":"Scholz used formal diplomatic and governmental processes before or alongside force-related support, but the supplied record does not establish that credible peaceful alternatives were fully tested or comparatively assessed. His September 2023 UN speech described prior Franco-German meetings with Moscow and Kyiv and support for the Copenhagen and Jeddah processes, while his October diplomacy with regional leaders sought to prevent escalation, secure hostage release, and enable humanitarian aid [BATCH-0013-E006][BATCH-0031-E002][BATCH-0033-E011]. The government also pursued allied coordination over Leopard authorization, and the Bundestag formally approved continued participation in SEA GUARDIAN after government reporting [BATCH-0013-E004][BATCH-0016-E003]. However, Scholz rejected an immediate Ukraine ceasefire unless it satisfied his stated conditions concerning freedom, justice, and territorial integrity, and the government rejected or abstained from ceasefire resolutions in the Israel-Hamas context while prioritizing support for Israel's defense [BATCH-0013-E006][BATCH-0011-R04-E005]. Parliamentary reporting also records criticism that the Ukraine weapons policy lacked a clear peace strategy, while Scholz initially resisted Leopard deliveries pending allied coordination [BATCH-0029-E010][BATCH-0031-E001]. These materials document diplomatic activity, formal procedures, policy criteria, and contested decisions—not the feasibility, seriousness, or comparative merits of all peaceful alternatives, nor successful settlement outcomes. Attribution is to Scholz where his actions or statements are directly reported, and otherwise to his government; the Ukraine case concerned support in an inherited Russian invasion rather than German initiation of force, within coalition and alliance
